segments.on_screen: Arrive: what antiBug is, two ways in, empty record
segments.text: I’m Ramy. I built antiBug for developers who use AI to write code and want to sharpen their debugging skills through short, timed challenges.

segments.on_screen: Try a sample (one click, no code needed), then Claude plants one bug and checks it still compiles
segments.text: I click “Try a sample.” Claude plants a bug for me to find.

segments.on_screen: Hunt: one line is broken, the clock is running
segments.text: Now the clock starts. I read the code and hunt for the faulty line.

segments.on_screen: Wrong guess: +10 s and a temperature hint
segments.text: That guess is wrong, so ten seconds are added. “Hot” tells me I’m close.

segments.on_screen: Hint: the bug's category for +15 s
segments.text: I take a hint. It helps, but adds another fifteen seconds.

segments.on_screen: Found it: click the broken line
segments.text: Found it. I click the faulty line.

segments.on_screen: Reveal: original and planted side by side, with the lesson
segments.text: I compare the original and changed code, then learn what went wrong and how to recognize that mistake.

segments.on_screen: Result: clock plus penalties, streak and best time
segments.text: My final time includes the penalties. I can track my streak and compare this result with my best time.

segments.on_screen: In the code: your click and the planted bug, labelled
segments.text: The “your click” and “planted bug” tags show exactly what I selected and where Claude placed the bug.

segments.on_screen: Drill again plants a new bug; or bring your own commit
segments.text: Next, I can drill again or practice with my own commit.
